label: a6-032-thm-compact-open-equals-compact-convergence
tail:
No fatal defects found. The proof is logically valid, all steps are justified by the cited dependencies, and the dependencies themselves supply exactly the required claims. The only potential issue is an unverifiable external claim in the Remarks.

### FINDING 1 — NONFATAL — location: Remarks, fourth paragraph (the final bullet)

CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "This is the theorem that lets the rest of the page use whichever description is convenient. The comparison of the three topologies is proved against compact convergence, while the evaluation map and the exponential law are proved against the compact-open topology, and the two are the same topology whenever both are defined."

WHY IT FAILS: The statement asserts facts about other items in the library (how the comparison of three topologies, the evaluation map, and the exponential law are proved, and that they rely on this theorem). The items referenced are not supplied in this audit, so the claim cannot be verified. It may be false, and as a remark about external items it is outside the scope of the present proof.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Either remove the claim, or phrase it as an intention/design note (e.g., “This equality allows the library to use the two descriptions interchangeably.”) instead of an assertion of fact about other items.

---

**Checked:** The entire proof, all eleven numbered steps, the handling of degenerate cases (empty K, V=Y), the construction of the covers and finite subcovers, the use of compactness (intrinsic and ambient forms), the application of the extreme value theorem, the distance‑function properties, the triangle inequality, the basis/sub‑basis generation arguments, and every [L#] fact against its verbatim dependency text. All dependencies supply exactly what is needed; no choice principle is required.

**0 fatal, 1 nonfatal**
